result.note: Tests the April 2026 renewal of the EIC certificate waiver for rice exports, its scope and the export figure.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's rice export policy as of April 2026:
items: India renewed a six-month waiver on mandatory inspection certificates for rice exports to non-EU European countries.
The waiver was first introduced in October 2024.
India's rice exports reached USD 12.95 billion in 2024-25, up 62% since 2014.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the waiver was first introduced in October 2025, not 2024. The renewal on 10 April 2026 clears the way for faster shipments to buyers across Eastern Europe and Eurasia.
questions.source: Last Friday, New Delhi renewed a six-month waiver on mandatory inspection certificates for rice exports to non-EU European countries, extending a policy first introduced in October 2025.

questions.prompt: Under India's rice export policy renewed in April 2026, the Export Inspection Council (EIC) certificate remains compulsory for rice exports to which of the following countries?
questions.explain: The EIC certificate remains compulsory for EU member states, the UK, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland, while all other European countries are exempt. TBB notes the exemption targets markets in Eurasia and the Balkans that do not demand Brussels-level paperwork.
questions.source: The Export Inspection Council (EIC) certificate remains compulsory for EU member states, the UK, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, and Switzerland.
